subject.title: fix(memory-wiki): skip malformed legacy import-run files in doctor

question: Should malformed legacy import-run files remain in place indefinitely, or should doctor reversibly quarantine them after warning so subsequent runs converge?
rationale: Both choices preserve user data, but they differ in repeated-warning behavior and how much doctor may mutate malformed legacy artifacts; repository history does not establish that policy.

options.title: Quarantine rejected files
options.body: Rename rejected JSON files to a reversible non-JSON quarantine form, warn with the new location, and prove a second doctor run is clean.

options.title: Retain and rewarn
options.body: Leave rejected files untouched and explicitly accept that every later doctor run will plan the migration and repeat the warning until manual cleanup.

recommendation.title: Quarantine rejected files
recommendation.body: Rename rejected JSON files to a reversible non-JSON quarantine form, warn with the new location, and prove a second doctor run is clean.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the affected migration and archive contract and are the strongest available history owner for its disposition policy.
